proposal: The Mandate recommends prohibiting the FBI, in general, from activities related to combating the spread of so-called misinformation and disinformation by Americans who are not tied to any plausible criminal activity. It also calls for a firewall at DOJ between legitimate activities, such as monitoring online activity for threats, and asking or demanding that forums or publishers remove material based on its content or viewpoint.

status_summary: Executive Order 14149, signed 2025-01-20 and published 2025-01-28, bars federal entities and personnel from acting or using federal resources contrary to its policy against abridging protected speech, and directs the Attorney General to review prior-administration activities that conflicted with it. In memoranda issued 2025-02-05 the Attorney General disbanded the Foreign Influence Task Force, which had alerted social media companies to foreign disinformation, according to press reporting. A specific written FBI prohibition or DOJ firewall policy was not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14149, Restoring Freedom of Speech and Ending Federal Censorship, was signed; it was published in the Federal Register on 2025-01-28.
An Attorney General memorandum disbanded the Foreign Influence Task Force, whose work had included alerting social media companies to foreign disinformation, according to press reporting.

title: Bar FBI activity aimed at policing speech and misinformation
uncertainties: The specific memorandum that disbanded the Foreign Influence Task Force was not identified; the cartel and integrity memoranda of the same date do not mention it, and the press report says only that it appeared in one of 14 memoranda issued that day. The task force was a foreign-influence unit, so its closure matches the recommendation only in part. No FBI-specific order or Justice Manual change was found.
